message.content:
Endel’s own material consistently describes its **core app soundscapes** (including Focus programs and “Deeper Focus”) as *real‑time, on‑device, generative assemblies of human‑made stems*, whereas its **albums/streaming releases** are explicitly described as *pre‑recorded, static audio*. The company does not appear to describe Deep/Deeper Focus as “non‑generative” or purely produced tracks; instead, it emphasizes that Plastikman’s stems are used inside a real‑time adaptive engine.[18][20][30] Third‑party reviewers generally echo this generative interpretation, though some focus more on the AI/generative aspect and others on the stem‑assembly aspect.[14][19][23][29]

Below I separate:  
- **Endel’s own documentation and statements**  
- **Third‑party claims**  
- **Any tensions/ambiguities**  
and address your four specific questions.

---

## 1) How Endel describes its core technology (generative engine vs curated stems)

### Endel’s own description

**Generative, real‑time, on‑device engine**

- Endel’s main site states that its patented technology “creates soundscapes that adapt in real-time” to inputs such as time of day, weather, heart rate, and location, and that “all sounds are generated in real-time, along with their signature visuals.”[10][17]  
- The “Soundscapes” page clarifies: “The Endel app has two main forms of audio content — Soundscapes and Scenarios. Soundscapes are endlessly generated on the device following your local inputs — weather, time of day, cadence of your walks, and heart rate…”[10][24]  
- The technology page for **Endel Pacific** (their AI engine) says it “can understand context, and generate the optimal soundscape for focus, relaxation, or sleep – in real-time, on-device.”[1][16]  
- The science page emphasizes that “All Endel sounds are generated using our proprietary, patented AI engine — Endel Pacific. This is how we get our soundscapes to be personalized to your inputs at all times, and endless.”[28]

Taken together, Endel’s own documentation describes the **core app soundscapes** as **endlessly generated, real‑time, on‑device audio that adapts to inputs**, not as simple playback of fixed tracks.[10][24][28]

**Role of stems and human-made material**

Endel also explicitly recognizes that the building blocks are **pre‑designed audio elements**:

- The technology page notes: “The sound logic and elements are pre-designed by our sound team and assigned to every soundscape. Driven by the core logic, with any input change the sound adapts on-the-fly.”[1]  
- The help center (“What is Endel”) explains that Endel’s sound engine consists of “sound layers, modulations, and effects” created in line with psychoacoustic studies, and an algorithm “constructs unique combinations of sound engine components” on the fly.[22][13]

So in Endel’s own framing:

- **Stems/elements**: Human-composed, pre‑designed audio components (layers, stems, effects).[1][13]  
- **Engine**: Algorithmic/AI system that assembles and modulates these components in real time based on user state and contextual inputs.[10][13][28]

**App vs streaming albums**

Endel makes a very explicit distinction between app soundscapes and streaming albums:

- Endel support: “The soundscapes in the Endel app are personalized and adaptive: they adapt in real-time to your location, weather, heart rate, motion, and circadian rhythm… The albums on streaming platforms are generated by the same technology … but they are pre-recorded and static.”[2]  
- Another help article on albums reiterates the albums are “pre-recorded and then released on streaming platforms as static albums.”[7]

In Endel’s own words, therefore:

- **App soundscapes** = realtime, adaptive, generative assemblies of pre‑designed elements.[10][13][22][28]  
- **Streaming albums** = pre‑recorded, static outputs of that technology.[2][7]

---

## 2) Are newer Focus programs like Deep/Deeper Focus, and artist collaborations, generated in real time or pre-produced tracks/loops?

Here it matters to distinguish:

- “Deep Focus” / “Deeper Focus” soundscape in the app  
- Artist collaboration soundscapes in the app  
- Their corresponding albums/playlist releases on streaming platforms

### Endel’s own statements on Focus soundscapes and Deep/Deeper Focus

**Core Focus soundscapes (including newer Focus programs)**

- Endel’s Focus page says: “Soundscapes are endlessly generated on the device following your local inputs — weather, time of day, cadence of your walks, and heart rate…”[21][24]  
- The main site describes four main modes (Focus, Relax, Sleep, Activity) as **soundscapes that adapt in real time**; Focus is one of these.[10][19]

There is **no carve‑out** in these official descriptions that says newer Focus variants (e.g. Deep Focus/Deeper Focus) behave differently from other Focus modes in the app. They are presented as part of the same real‑time soundscape system.[10][21][24]

**Endel × Plastikman / Deeper Focus collaboration**

Endel’s own press and help center are explicit:

- Press release for the Plastikman collaboration: “Endel… has partnered with… Plastikman… to release their collaborative AI-powered soundscape ‘Deeper Focus’… Hawtin worked extensively with Endel’s… AI… to produce a personalized, real-time adaptive soundscape… These stems were then processed by Endel AI to create a soundscape that adapts in real-time to the user’s location, weather, natural light exposure, and with beats synced to heart rate.”[18]  
- Endel’s help article “Endel × Plastikman”: “It pairs original sounds by Plastikman with Endel AI to generate an endless functional soundscape that adapts in real-time to your location, weather, heart rate, and natural light exposure.”[20]  
- An interview on Beatportal quoting Endel directly: “Deeper Focus is an endless soundscape that is generated in real-time using AI. The AI takes inputs like location, weather, natural light, and heart rate, then creates the optimum personalized sound environment… using audio stems created by Plastikman.”[30]

These statements are clear that:

- Richie Hawtin/Plastikman **creates stems**.  
- Endel AI **generates an endless, real‑time adaptive soundscape** from those stems in the app.[18][20][30]

There is no language here suggesting that in‑app Deeper Focus is just a fixed playlist or a set of loops played back without adaptation.

### Artist collaborations generally

While you asked specifically about Deep Focus, the same pattern appears in Endel’s general explanatory materials:

- Endel’s technology page: sound logic and elements are pre‑designed and assigned to each soundscape, then the core logic adapts on-the-fly.[1]  
- Their press materials for collaborations (e.g., Amazon sleep playlists, focus soundscapes) describe the use of Endel Pacific to generate personalized soundtracks that follow sleep phases or adapt in real time, even when based on artist-supplied sounds.[6][27]

Thus, for collaborations **inside the app**:

- Endel’s own messaging consistently describes them as **adaptive, endlessly generated soundscapes using artist-provided stems
